verdicts.text: You must use methods supplied in the Pulumi SDK to access an output's value once it is known.
verdicts.evidence: The Node.js SDK's Output class blocks direct string conversion and points users to SDK methods. From the decoded source: "Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported. To get the value of an Output<T> as an Output<string> consider either: 1: o.apply(v => `prefix${v}suffix`) 2: pulumi.interpolate". Its docs also say "the value an Output points to is asynchronously computed", which matches the doc's statement that you need apply/all/helpers to get at an output's value.
verdicts.framing_note: Checked only against the Node.js SDK. The Python, Go, and .NET SDKs follow the same Output/apply design.

verdicts.text: Secrets have the same type, Output<T>, as unencrypted resource outputs, differing only in being marked internally as needing encryption before persisting in the state file.
verdicts.evidence: The Node.js SDK's Output class has an internal `isSecret` flag. Its doc comment says: "Whether or not this output wraps a secret value. Values which are marked as secret are stored in an encrypted format when they are persisted as part of a state file." So a secret is a normal Output<T> with an internal marker, which matches the claim.
verdicts.framing_note: Checked against the Node.js SDK only. Other SDKs have the same design, but I didn't check their source here.

verdicts.text: In every Pulumi language, an unhandled error raised inside an `apply` callback is reported as a deployment failure, causing `pulumi up` to abort the update and print the error in its diagnostics.
verdicts.evidence: I couldn't check this against product source because GitHub code search hit its rate limit. The page qualifies the "every language" wording itself. L631 says the error "is not swallowed (with one Go-specific exception described below)", and the Go warning at L685 says an error from an `ApplyT` whose output is discarded "is silently dropped and the update succeeds". So the universal claim as extracted conflicts with the page's own Go caveat.
verdicts.source: repo:content/docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply.md L631, L685; gh search code (HTTP 403 rate limit)
verdicts.intuition_flag: The "in every Pulumi language" wording is too broad. The page says Go does not fail the update when an ApplyT output is never consumed, so the sentence should keep the Go qualifier next to it.

verdicts.text: Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference says `pulumi package publish` will "Publish a package to the Private Registry... The package can be a provider or a schema." It also says that when given a PLUGIN reference it resolves or installs a resource plugin, and that "When <provider> is specified as a local path, Pulumi executes the provider binary to extract its package schema." That means executable (binary plugin) packages can be published to the Private Registry, which is part of Pulumi Cloud.
